title: The specified Frobenius tensor comparison preserves the intrinsic completion unit
statement:
Fix primes $p\ne\ell$, $q=p^a$ with $a\ge1$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{k_0}$, an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a finite intermediate field $E\subset\Omega$, with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $W_0$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme, $W=W_0\times_{k_0}k$, and $B=\varprojlim_{n\ge1}(R/\varpi^n)_W$ on the small pro-etale site. Use the integral category $\mathcal I_E=D^b_c(W_{\mathrm{proet}},R)$ of [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete], whose raw rationalization is the coefficient category of [def-wf-weil-category].
Let $\Phi_W=\mathrm{id}_{W_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(z\mapsto z^{1/q})$ and let $H=\Phi_W^*$ be exact integral coefficient transport [def-wf-weil-category]. Write $C(A)=A^{\wedge}_{\mathrm{Kos}}$ and $\eta_A:A\to C(A)$ for [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion]. For $M,N\in\mathcal I_E$ put $T=M\otimes_B^L N$ and $T'=HM\otimes_B^L HN$. Let $a:HT\xrightarrow{\sim}T'$ and $b:HC(T)\xrightarrow{\sim}C(T')$ be respectively the specified ordinary and completed tensor/pullback comparisons of [def-wf-tensor-product], with the coefficient isomorphism induced by the constant finite quotient maps. Then in $D(B)$
$$b\circ H(\eta_T)=\eta_{T'}\circ a.$$
The equality holds already on the specified flat-term K-flat models: for representatives $U,V$, set $A=\operatorname{Tot}(U\otimes_B V)$ and $A'=\operatorname{Tot}(HU\otimes_B HV)$, and use $Q_m=[B\xrightarrow{\varpi^m}B]$ in degrees $[-1,0]$, with transition $\varpi$ in degree $-1$ and identity in degree zero. Under the canonical maps $HQ_m\cong Q_m$ and $H\prod_m\cong\prod_m H$, the chain maps representing $a,b$ satisfy $bH(\eta_A)=\eta_{A'}a$. Here the two units are the actual maps $z\mapsto((z\otimes\iota_m)_m,0)$ into the product mapping-fiber complexes, with $\iota_m:B[0]\to Q_m$ the degree-zero inclusion. This also specifies the equality after localization of the models at quasi-isomorphisms.

Its hypotheses hold: W is of finite type over k and ℓ≠p. The citer already quantifies over integral D^b_c(W,O_E), and the conclusion is unchanged, so nothing is weakened. Step 1: the inverse-image lemma (clause 2) gives exactness and preservation of products. def-wf-tensor-product specifies c, the balanced iso α, and that they represent the derived comparison. The ringed-topoi lemma gives flat-term K-flat preservation. Step 2: c(ϖ)=ϖ and c(1)=1, so β_m H(1⊗ι_m)=(1⊗ι_m)α on generators, and the transition (ϖ in degree −1, identity in degree 0) commutes. Step 3: pr_m δ H(u_A)=pr_m u_{A'} α, and the product's universal property gives δ H(u_A)=u_{A'} α. On F=B⊕B[−1], b sends (H u_A z,0) to (u_{A'} α z,0), a strict chain equality. Step 4: localization. The intrinsic-completion hypotheses hold for O_E with I=(ϖ).
